claims.statement: resolve_github_token reads authoritative thread metadata: public threads use a GitHub App installation token, while a private thread can resolve dashboard OAuth only for its saved owner when that owner started the run.
When a private thread's validated credential owner has no valid dashboard GitHub token, resolve_github_token raises GitHubUserAuthRequired rather than silently falling back to the GitHub App token.

Resolved GitHub tokens are cached only in process memory keyed by (thread_id, principal), where normalized login:/email: principals isolate personal tokens and a distinct bot principal isolates installation tokens; caching an unbound user token is refused.

Personal cached GitHub tokens expire on their own expiry with a 60-second skew or after a hard 24-hour TTL; expired bot entries remain only until that TTL cap so they can be reminted with their recorded repository scope, and invalidate_cached_github_token clears a thread's entries.

GitHub App installation tokens are cached only in process memory by installation id, repository ids/names, and permissions, and are reused only until within a 10-minute margin of their reported expiry; unavailable App configuration returns no token except for the local gh CLI development fallback.

LangSmith sandbox proxy rules inject a GitHub App installation token on the wire as opaque Authorization headers for api.github.com and github.com while the sandbox only sees a placeholder GH_TOKEN; proxy refresh preserves recorded repository and permission scope and a before-model middleware refreshes near-expiry tokens.

The dashboard authenticates browsers through GitHub OAuth and an HS256 osw_session JWT signed with DASHBOARD_JWT_SECRET and valid for seven days; require_session rejects a missing session cookie and /me returns the signed-in identity plus is_admin.

The OAuth login/callback flow binds a random state nonce to the browser: /auth/login stores the nonce HMAC in a signed state JWT and the raw nonce in a cookie, and /auth/callback verifies them with a constant-time compare before exchanging the code, enforcing the login gate, persisting OAuth tokens, and issuing a session.

Post-login redirects are constrained by sanitize_redirect_to, which permits only same-origin relative paths or origins on the dashboard allowlist (DASHBOARD_BASE_URL plus DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) and blocks login and dashboard API paths, preventing an OAuth flow from being steered to an attacker origin or callback loop.

Dashboard login admission requires a configured ALLOWED_GITHUB_USERS or ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS allowlist unless local auth is enabled at startup; a listed login is accepted, while organization membership is checked with a GitHub App installation token with members: read and API/token/membership failures deny access.

Cookie-authenticated dashboard mutations are CSRF-protected by an origin allowlist: safe methods are exempt and a request whose only credential is an explicit bearer GitHub token without a session cookie is exempt because a browser cannot forge it.

Desktop login uses PKCE so no session is placed on a loopback URL: the browser receives a 120-second handoff JWT carrying identity and the app's S256 challenge, and redeem_desktop_handoff mints the session only when presented the matching verifier via constant-time compare; cloud-terminal access uses a 60-second ticket bound to a specific thread_id and audience.
Slack accounts are linked to GitHub identities through verified Slack OIDC, and verify_team refuses identities from a different workspace when SLACK_TEAM_ID is configured.

Auth-failure notices posted into a shared Slack thread are token-free and link only to build_settings_url() rather than a per-user GitHub auth URL, so nobody else in the thread can complete auth and bind the wrong account.

verify_github_signature authenticates GitHub webhooks by recomputing sha256=HMAC(GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, body) and comparing to X-Hub-Signature-256 with constant-time compare, failing closed when the secret is unset, and the GitHub webhook route rejects failures before parsing the payload.

verify_slack_signature validates the v0:timestamp:body HMAC against the Slack signature and additionally rejects requests whose timestamp is older than 300 seconds to block replay, failing closed when the signing secret is unset.

verify_linear_signature authenticates Linear webhooks by comparing the raw-body HMAC-SHA256 against the Linear-Signature header with constant-time compare, failing closed when LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset.

The publicly reachable /webhooks/run-complete route is authenticated by verify_run_complete_token against a shared secret (RUN_COMPLETE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) using constant-time compare, and is fail-closed: when the secret is unset every call is rejected and run-failure replies are disabled.

Persisted credentials are encrypted at rest with a MultiFernet built from TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which may be a most-recent-first key list so the first key encrypts and every key is tried for decryption to enable rotation; decrypt_token degrades to an empty string on an invalid token or missing key rather than raising.

When GitHub reports an unrecoverable refresh error (bad_refresh_token or unauthorized_client), the stored GitHub OAuth authorization is dropped unless a concurrent callback has replaced it, so callers prompt a clean re-login instead of serving a known-stale access token.

Admin identity is derived from CONFIGURED_ADMINS matched case-insensitively on email or login, and require_admin re-checks the triggering user or authorized scheduled run at tool-call time rather than trusting thread metadata.

Untrusted external GitHub comment content is wrapped in reserved <dangerous-external-untrusted-users-comment> trust tags, and sanitize_github_comment_body strips those reserved tags from raw comment bodies so external content cannot spoof the trust wrapper.

Dashboard origin enforcement has an explicit local-development fail-open default: require_same_origin does nothing if no DASHBOARD_BASE_URL or DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS origin is configured; otherwise unsafe cookie-authenticated requests need an allowed Origin/Referer, while create_app enables credentialed CORS only for configured origins and rejects a wildcard origin.

Dashboard session cookies are HttpOnly; HTTPS split-origin dashboard use produces Secure, SameSite=None session cookies, while same-origin or local HTTP uses SameSite=Lax, and the OAuth state cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, auth-path scoped, and limited to the state TTL.

Focused tests cover OAuth redirect allowlisting, state and desktop PKCE protections; public/private thread credential and PR-author scope; sandbox proxy injection; and proxy expiry refresh middleware.
